summary: A reminder from BBN about scheduled IMP software releases. IMPs can be reloaded between 7 and 8 a.m. Eastern time every Tuesday, in addition to hardware maintenance. An IMP going down message is sent to all hosts at the site about an hour before.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC reminds network hosts about the weekly time reserved for IMP software maintenance. It explains what advance notices say and how a final warning is sent before an IMP goes down.

subtitle: A reminder of the IMP maintenance window and host warning messages.

tldr.problem: Hosts needed a predictable schedule and advance notice for IMP software maintenance.
tldr.mechanism: BBN reserves 7 to 8 a.m. Eastern time every Tuesday and sends IMP-Going-Down messages with timing, duration and reason.
tldr.outcome: The RFC re-emphasizes the procedures in RFC 381 and updates that RFC according to the unit metadata.

facts.label: Reserved window
facts.value: 7 to 8 a.m. Eastern time every Tuesday

today: The unit metadata lists RFC 406 as Unknown and says it updates RFC 381. It documents an early ARPANET maintenance procedure.

sections.title: The Scheduled Window
sections.content:
The note says the scheduling procedures proposed in RFC 381 had been in effect for about two months. BBN reserves 7 to 8 a.m. Eastern time every Tuesday for possible IMP software reloads, although the period may not be used every week.

This software maintenance time is separate from hardware preventive maintenance scheduled at each site.
sections.plainLanguage: One hour every Tuesday is reserved for IMP software reloads. BBN may not use the hour each week, and hardware maintenance is scheduled separately.

sections.title: Advance and Final Notices
sections.content:
BBN sends an IMP-Going-Down message to all Hosts at a site with the time, expected duration and reason. BBN tries to send the notice an hour before software releases and five to ten minutes before scheduled preventive maintenance.

When possible, Hosts are also notified before an unscheduled stop. Thirty seconds before the IMP goes down, a second message says that the shutdown is immediate.
sections.plainLanguage: Hosts receive a notice with the expected timing, duration and reason. A second message arrives 30 seconds before shutdown.

sections.title: Message Fields
sections.content:
The IMP-Going-Down message has 32 bits. Bits 1 through 4 are zero, bits 5 through 8 are 0010, and bits 9 through 16 are zero.

Bits 17 and 18 identify scheduled hardware maintenance, scheduled software reload or emergency reload on restart. Bits 19 through 22 say how soon the IMP will go down in 5-minute units; bits 23 through 32 give the expected downtime in 5-minute units. All bits zero means going down in 30 seconds.
sections.plainLanguage: The message uses fields for the reason, how soon the IMP will stop and how long it will be down. The time values use five-minute units, except for the all-zero signal that means 30 seconds.

fields.name: Reason
fields.desc: Bits 17 and 18: 01 hardware PM, 10 software reload, 11 emergency reload.

references.text: RFC 381, the maintenance scheduling procedures re-emphasized by RFC 406.
